test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a circle with centre O, AOC is the diameter. B is a point on the circumference of the circle such that arc AB is (1/5) of the arc BC. What is the degree measure of angleBOC?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The central angle subtended by an arc is directly proportional to its arc length.

Given the ratio of Arc AB to Arc BC is 1 : 5, the ratio of their central angles ∠AOB : ∠BOC is also 1 : 5.

Since AOC is a diameter, the total angle on the straight line is 180°.

∠BOC = [5 ÷ (1 + 5)] × 180°

∠BOC = (5 ÷ 6) × 180° = 150°.

**∴ The correct answer is 150°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AOC is the diameter of the circle with centre O.

Arc AB = (1 ÷ 5) × Arc BC

**Concept Used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is directly proportional to the length of the arc.

The angle of a straight line (diameter) at the centre is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e45e140ba434bd89b0162d68ccae719ecd7865c381cf4758a62171218710d2b.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the length of Arc AB be x.

⇒ Then, the length of Arc BC = 5x.

⇒ Ratio of ∠AOB to ∠BOC = Arc AB : Arc BC = x : 5x = 1 : 5.

⇒ Let ∠AOB = k and ∠BOC = 5k.

⇒ Since AOC is a straight line, the sum of angles on one side is 180°.

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠BOC = 180°

⇒ k + 5k = 180°

⇒ 6k = 180°

⇒ k = 30°

⇒ Therefore, ∠BOC = 5k = 5 × 30° = 150°

**∴ The correct answer is 150°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arc and Angle Proportion Rule

In any given circle, the central angle subtended by an arc is completely proportional to its physical arc length. (∠ ∝ Arc length).

Semicircle Property

The arc of a semicircle subtends exactly 180° at the centre of the circle and 90° at any point on the remaining circumference.

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is exactly double the angle subtended by the same arc at any remaining part of the circle's boundary.
